source.publication: Instructions for 2025 PIT-ADJ; 2025 PIT-1 Personal Income Tax Return Instructions; 2025 Tax Rate Table (Tax Look Up Table)
source.section: PIT-ADJ instructions PDF page 5, line 16; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12; Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 50,000.00 + long-term gains 20,000.00 = 70,000.00. Federal taxable income = 70,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 54,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, single. Line 9 federal AGI 70,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 15,750.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 70,000.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 36,667.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 16 net capital gains: smaller of 20,000.00 and the cap 2,500.00 = 2,500.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 2,500.00. Line 17 = 70,000.00 + 0.00 - 15,750.00 - 0.00 - 2,500.00 = 51,750.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 54,250.00 - 2,500.00 = 51,750.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 51,750.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 5,500.00 = 82.5 + 3.2% x 11,000.00 = 352 + 4.3% x 17,000.00 = 731 + 4.7% x 18,250.00 = 857.75; total 2,023.25, to the cent 2,023.25. The table row over 51,700 to 51,800 gives 2,023; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 2,023.25. The 40% alternative is only for the sale of a business (not_modelled); these gains are from securities, so the 2,500.00 is the larger.
